hints: Find the total distance travelled along the track by adding the lengths of both ramps: $d_{\text{total}} = 8 + 10 = 18\text{ m}$.
The resistance force has constant magnitude $640\text{ N}$ throughout.
walkthrough:
Calculate the total distance travelled along the ramps:
$$d_{\text{total}} = 8 + 10 = 18\text{ m}$$

Calculate the work done against the constant resistance force of $640\text{ N}$:
$$W_{\text{res}} = F_{\text{res}} \times d_{\text{total}} = 640 \times 18 = 11520\text{ J}$$
teacher_walkthrough:
State the formula for work done against a constant resistance force along the path of motion:
$$W_{\text{res}} = F_{\text{res}} \times d$$

Calculate the total distance moved along the surface of both ramps:
$$d = 8\text{ m} + 10\text{ m} = 18\text{ m}$$

Multiply the resistance force by this total distance:
$$W_{\text{res}} = 640 \times 18 = 11520\text{ J}$$

hints: Calculate initial kinetic energy at the bottom of the first ramp: $E_{k1} = \frac{1}{2}(840)(14^2) = 82320\text{ J}$.
Determine net vertical height change from bottom of first ramp to bottom of second ramp: $h = 8\sin 30^\circ - 10\sin 20^\circ = 4 - 3.4202 = 0.5798\text{ m}$ above initial level.
Calculate net potential energy gained: $\Delta E_p = 840 \times 10 \times 0.5798 = 4870\text{ J}$.
Apply the work-energy balance: $E_{k2} = E_{k1} - \Delta E_p - W_{\text{res}} = 82320 - 4870 - 11520 = 65930\text{ J}$, and solve for $v$.
walkthrough:
Calculate the initial kinetic energy of the car at the bottom of the first ramp with $u = 14\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$E_{k1} = \frac{1}{2}m u^2 = \frac{1}{2} \times 840 \times 14^2 = 420 \times 196 = 82320\text{ J}$$

Determine the net gain in gravitational potential energy between the start and end points:
$$\Delta E_p = mg(8\sin 30^\circ - 10\sin 20^\circ) = 8400(4 - 3.42020) = 8400(0.57980) \approx 4870.3\text{ J}$$

Apply the work-energy equation, taking into account the work done against resistance ($11520\text{ J}$) from part (i):
$$E_{k2} = E_{k1} - \Delta E_p - W_{\text{res}}$$
$$\frac{1}{2}(840)v^2 = 82320 - 4870.3 - 11520 = 65929.7\text{ J}$$

Solve for the final speed $v$:
$$420v^2 = 65929.7 \implies v^2 = \frac{65929.7}{420} \approx 156.975$$
$$v = \sqrt{156.975} \approx 12.529\text{ m s}^{-1} \approx 12.5\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
teacher_walkthrough:
State the work-energy balance for the roller-coaster car:
$$\text{Final KE} = \text{Initial KE} - \text{Net PE Gain} - \text{Work Done Against Resistance}$$

Calculate the initial kinetic energy:
$$E_{k1} = \frac{1}{2}mu^2 = \frac{1}{2} \times 840 \times (14)^2 = 420 \times 196 = 82320\text{ J}$$

Find the vertical height gained on the ascent and lost on the descent:
$$h_{\text{ascent}} = 8\sin 30^\circ = 8 \times 0.5 = 4\text{ m}$$
$$h_{\text{descent}} = 10\sin 20^\circ \approx 10 \times 0.342020 = 3.42020\text{ m}$$
$$h_{\text{net}} = 4 - 3.42020 = 0.57980\text{ m}$$

Calculate the net potential energy increase:
$$\Delta E_p = mgh_{\text{net}} = 840 \times 10 \times 0.57980 = 8400 \times 0.57980 \approx 4870.32\text{ J}$$

Substitute the energies into the work-energy equation with $W_{\text{res}} = 11520\text{ J}$:
$$\frac{1}{2}(840)v^2 = 82320 - 4870.32 - 11520$$
$$420v^2 = 65929.68$$

Take the square root to find the final speed:
$$v = \sqrt{156.9754} \approx 12.5290\text{ m s}^{-1} = 12.5\text{ m s}^{-1} \text{ (to 3 s.f.)}$$
